source.title: Written in Trade Today
source.summary: Series finale: five Arabic words, five centuries, five lessons for the trade wars of 2025.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: In this series finale, we return to the present moment. As tariff walls rise and supply chains fragment, what would a medieval Karimi merchant say about the trade wars of 2025? Five words. Five lessons: transparency works, credit needs trust, maritime freedom benefits all, infrastructure is a public good, and risk should be shared. The principles hidden in our vocabulary are whispering. Are we listening?

x.single_post: The Arabic word 'tariff' comes from ta'rifa, meaning 'to make known.' Medieval merchants demanded transparency in what they would pay. We forgot this and turned tariffs into weapons.
thread: The Arabic word 'tariff' comes from ta'rifa, meaning 'to make known.' Medieval merchants demanded transparency in what they would pay.
Credit comes from qirad, the Islamic partnership where one person provides capital, another provides work. Trust was built into the word itself.
Arsenal comes from dar as-sina'a, the house of industry. Venice learned shipbuilding from Muslim engineers and built an empire on their blueprints.
Five Arabic words in our trade vocabulary. Five lessons medieval merchants understood that we're forgetting in 2025. https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-tt-6

Arsenal comes from dar as-sina'a, the house of industry. Venice learned shipbuilding from Muslim engineers and built a maritime empire on their blueprints. As tariff walls rise in 2025, our trade vocabulary whispers lessons from five centuries ago: transparency works, credit needs trust, infrastructure is a public good. The principles are hidden in plain sight, embedded in the words we use every day. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-tt-6
